answer: Because next-hop state hangs off the RIB. In `show next-hop`, each entry represents a RIB identified by the 'name' key, and all routes in a RIB belong to the same address family. For each routing instance the system provides one system-controlled default RIB per supported address family, so the next-hop for a prefix is only meaningful within its RIB. Syntax: `show next-hop-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>/<interface> [next-hop-address]`. rib-name is a String (length 1..64, pattern '([A-Za-z0-9 -.,]*)'), destination-prefix is an IP prefix, interface is the outgoing interface name (for example DCN), and next-hop-address is an IPv4 or IPv6 address. Example: `show next-hop-IPv4/0.0.0.0/0/DCN`. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use `clear [-f] ospf [instance=]<value>`. This removes and restarts the ospf-instance, and the operation is asynchronous, so the command returns without waiting for the restart to complete. The instance id is a string and is supplied as <instance>. The `-f` flag forces the command without confirmation; without it you are prompted. Access mode is Operational Mode only. Example: `clear ospf 1`. To create, modify or delete the instance itself instead, use the ospf-instance commands (`add/set/show/delete ospf-instance-<instance-id>`).

No. The ospf-area object accepts only one area type: `ospf-area-type` has the single permitted value `normal`, and `normal` is also the default. There is no stub or NSSA option. Commands: `add|set ospf-area-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id> [ospf-area-type <value>]`, `show ospf-area-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id> [ospf-area-type]`, `delete ospf-area-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>`. instance-id is uint8 (range 0..255) and ospf-area-id is a dotted-quad. Pre-condition: the OSPF instance must be created before the area can be added. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: `add ospf-area-1/0.0.0.0`.

Use ospf-area-range, which summarizes routes for an OSPF area matching address/mask. It is applicable to Area Border Routers (ABRs) only, so it has no effect on a non-ABR. Syntax: `add|set ospf-area-range-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<prefix> [advertise <value>]`, `show ... [advertise]`, `delete ospf-area-range-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<prefix>`. prefix is an IPv4 prefix (length <= 32) or IPv6 prefix (length <= 128) in canonical form. `advertise` takes true or false and defaults to true (true advertises the summary, false hides it). Pre-condition: the OSPF instance must be created first. Example: `add ospf-area-range-1/9.9.9.9/10.220.0.0/16 advertise true`.

Yes. `add ospf-instance-<instance-id> router-id <value> [version <value>] [description <value>] [router-id-mode <value>]` accepts `version` values ospfv2 or ospfv3, with ospfv2 as the default; version is settable at add and is shown with `show ospf-instance-<instance-id> [version]`. instance-id is uint8 (range 0..255) and router-id is a dotted-quad. The router id source is `router-id-mode`, values manual or use-loopback, default use-loopback. Pre-condition: if router-id-mode is use-loopback, an ipv4 LO-MGMT address must be configured. `description` is a String (length 0..128). Example: `add ospf-instance-2 description xyz router-id-mode use-loopback version ospfv3`.

On ospf-interface the defaults are hello-interval 10 seconds (uint16, range 1..32767) and router-dead-interval 40 seconds (uint16, range 4..65535). Related defaults: retransmission-interval 5 s (2..3600), transmit-delay 1 s (1..450), ospf-cost 10 (1..65535), priority 1 (0..255, where 0 means not eligible for DR/BDR), enable true, ospf-if-routing auto (active, passive, auto). Authentication is available: `ospf-auth-enable` true/false, default false (relevant for ospfv2 or ospfv3); `ospf-auth-algorithm` none or HMAC_SHA_256, default HMAC_SHA_256; `ospf-auth-key` an ASCII string of length 0..256. The algorithm and key are only of relevance for ospfv2. Pre-condition: the OSPF instance and OSPF area must exist before adding the interface.

Use `show ospf-neighbor-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<router-id> [state] [role] [address] [priority]` (Operational Mode). The `state` values are: down (initial state, no Hello packets received from the neighbor), init (Hellos received but bidirectional communication not yet established), 2-way (bidirectional communication established, DR/BDR election occurs here), exstart (DR and BDR elected, master-slave relation determined), exchange (neighbors exchange DataBaseDescriptor (DBD) packets containing LSA headers), loading (routers exchange full Link State information based on DBDs), full (full adjacency achieved). The `role` values are drother (Designated Router Other), dr (Designated Router), bdr (Backup Designated Router) and ptp (point-to-point). Note: an OSPF neighbor is deleted when the OSPF interface is down.

Use ospfv3-ipsec-security-association: `add ospfv3-ipsec-security-association-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<spi> integrity-algorithm <value> [ipsec-protocol <value>] [ipsec-mode <value>]`, plus set/show/delete. The SPI is a unique uint32 in range 256..4294967295. integrity-algorithm is mandatory on add and takes AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128, AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_384_192, AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_512_256, AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_160 or AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96. ipsec-protocol indicates ESP or AH but the only value is ESP (default ESP), and ipsec-mode supports only transport (default transport). Pre-condition: the OSPF instance must be created first. Example: `add ospfv3-ipsec-security-association-1/0.0.0.0/DCN/256 integrity-algorithm AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128`.

Use `ping [-c=<count>] [-w=<timeout>] [-s=<pktsize>] [-i=<interface> | -v=<vrf>] <ping-dest>`. `-i=<interface>` specifies the source interface; by default the interface is selected according to the routing table. `-v=<vrf>` specifies the VRF; by default the MGMT VRF is used. The interface and VRF name parameters are mutually exclusive. `-c=<count>` stops after sending count ECHO_REQUEST packets, `-w=<timeout>` sets a timeout in seconds before ping exits regardless of packets sent or received, and `-s=<pktsize>` sets the octets sent exclusive of headers, default 56, plus 8 octets of ICMP header for a total of 64 octets. ping-dest may be an ipv4-address, ipv6-address or domain-name. Example: `ping -c=1 -w=10 -s=1024 192.0.2.3`.

`show protocols` lists them all in one place. Syntax: `show protocols [ssh|cli|serial-console|netconf|grpc|snmp|restconf|http-file-server|data-model-openconfig]`, available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Plain `show protocols` returns the nine containers: ssh, cli, serial-console, netconf, restconf, grpc, snmp, http-file-server and data-model-openconfig. Adding a keyword shows that protocol's detail, for example ssh with enabled and port 8022 plus host keys and pre/post-login messages, cli enabled true on port 22 with script-dir '/storage/scripts', netconf enabled true port 830, restconf http-port 8080 and https-port 8181 with cookie-timeout 5 minutes and api-root '/restconf', grpc port 50051, snmp port 161 with snmp-engine-id, http-file-server http-port 8980 and https-port 8981 with url-base '/transfer', and serial-console global-switch enabled with global-timeout 60 minutes.

Use `show rib-<rib-name> [vrf] [address-family]`, available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Each entry represents a RIB identified by the 'name' key and all routes in a RIB belong to the same address family; for each routing instance the system provides one system-controlled default RIB for each supported address family. rib-name is a String (length 1..64). The `address-family` attribute takes ipv4-unicast or ipv6-unicast, and `vrf` is a leafref to ../../vrf/name showing the VRF the RIB is bound to. Example: `show rib-IPv4` displays the RIB identified by the 'IPv4' key.

Use `show route-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix> [special-next-hop] [source-protocol]`. The `source-protocol` attribute gives the source protocol for the route entry, for example OSPF, BGP or static, so it distinguishes dynamic protocol routes from static configuration. The command shows the list of system routes from various sources, such as dynamic protocols and static routes. rib-name is a String (length 1..64) and destination-prefix is an IPv4 or IPv6 address. `special-next-hop` applies to IPv4/IPv6 static routes, rib:routes and IP Monitoring, with values none (default, no special treatment, used for all normal routes), blackhole and unreachable; for blackhole and unreachable routes no next-hop is created under the route. Example: `show route`.

Yes. `show routing` shows routing information. It takes no parameters at all and is available in both Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For more detail, drill into the related commands: `show rib-<rib-name> [vrf] [address-family]` for the RIB per address family, `show route-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix> [special-next-hop] [source-protocol]` for the route list including its source protocol, `show next-hop-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>/<interface> [next-hop-address]` for next hops, and `show vrf-<name> [type] [chassis-name] [description]` for the routing instances.

`show supporting-interface-<name>/<interface>` shows supporting interface information, that is which underlying IPv4/IPv6 interface supports a given interface. It has two parameters: `name`, the name of the interface (string), and `interface`, a reference to the IPv4/IPv6 interface, expressed as a path with the value ../../../../../networking/interface/if-name. Both are used only with show. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

`traceroute [-m=<hopcnt>] [-w=<timeout>] [-i=<interface> | -v=<vrf>] <tr-dest> [pktsize]` probes a maximum of 30 hops by default; `-m=<hopcnt>` is uint8 in range 1..255 and sets the maximum number of hops (max time-to-live). The VRF is MGMT by default: `-v=<vrf>` specifies the VRF and, if not provided, defaults to MGMT. `-i=<interface>` sets the source interface, which by default is selected according to the routing table, and the interface and VRF name parameters are mutually exclusive. `-w=<timeout>` is uint16 in range 1..10 seconds, default 2. pktsize is the total probing packet size, uint16 (60 bytes for IPv4), default 60. Example: `traceroute -m=10 -w=3 1.2.3.4`.

Use `show vrf-<name> [type] [chassis-name] [description]`, available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. `name` is the VRF name, a String of length 0..32. `chassis-name` gives the associated chassis name for that VRF. `type` reports the VRF type with values mgmt (Management VRF) or internal (Internal VRF). `description` is a String of length 0..255 describing the VRF and its intended purpose. Running `show vrf` without a key lists the instances; to view one, for example the management VRF, use `show vrf-MGMT`.

A successful swimage activation implies a system restart. Syntax: `activate [-f] swimage [label <string>] [db-action <empty-db|upgrade-db|rollback|auto>]`, Operational Mode. The optional `db-action` selects what happens to the database: auto (default) activates the image processing the database with the system default behavior, empty-db activates with an empty database, upgrade-db activates by upgrading the current database, and rollback rolls back to the previous active software image. If db-action is not provided the system decides automatically. Unless `-f` is given, the user must confirm the activation when prompted. `label` names the sw image/manifest file; if not specified the currently installable image is used. Example: `activate swimage db-action=empty-db`.

No. Only a single location led test can be running at a time, and not all cards support the Location LED test functionality. Syntax: `activate location-led [entity=]<value> [[timeout=]<value>] [[led-mode=]<value>]`, Operational Mode. `entity` is a chassis or a card. `led-mode` is flash (default, amber light blinking at 1 Hz, used for LED location) or solid (steady amber, used for lamp test); in lamp test all chassis LEDs light amber. To turn it off use `terminate location-led [entity=]<value>`, or set `timeout` in the range 0..120 seconds; the default timeout is 0, meaning no timeout and the function runs until terminated. Note: the timeout parameter does not take effect in 1830 GX G30 R5.1, so use terminate there. Example: `activate location-led card-1-1`.

Use the `bootstrap` command, which establishes a TLS connection over the OSC link and provisions the initial administrator account on a neighbor NE that has no configured users yet. Syntax: `bootstrap ([local-port=]<value> | [neighbor-address=]<value>) [new-admin-user=]<value> [new-password=]<value>`, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. Select the neighbor either by `local-port`, the supporting-port of a MGMT vrf osc-eth interface as shown in `show interface` (e.g. 1-1-dwdm-line1), which the system maps to the OCE netdev (OCE-<chassis>-<slot>-<vlan-id>) and resolves into neighbor-address via get_osc_neighbors.sh, or by `neighbor-address` directly, the IPv6 link-local address of the OSC peer including zone (string length 7..256, pattern 'fe80:.*'). If resolution fails the RPC is rejected. `new-admin-user` is mandatory, length 1..32, obeying local user naming rules. `new-password` may be plain text (standard complexity rules apply) or a $<id>$<salt>$<hash> hash, only id 6 (SHA512), salt 2..16 chars.

Type `cancel-upgrade`. The full syntax is `cancel-upgrade [-h]`, where `-h` just displays help for the command. It cancels any active upgrade in progress. Access mode is Operational mode. Pre-condition: an upgrade must be in progress for this command to execute successfully.

`change-ztp-mode enabled` starts ZTP, reverts the database to the factory default and triggers a system reboot, so re-enabling it on an in-service node wipes the configuration. Syntax: `change-ztp-mode [-f] [ztp-mode=]<value>` with ztp-mode values enabled or disabled, Operational mode; `-f` forces the command without confirmation, so without it you are prompted first. `change-ztp-mode disabled` disables ZTP and stops ZTP if it is already in progress; the command can be executed while ZTP is running, interrupting it. Use `show ztp` to display the current ZTP mode configuration. Example: `change-ztp-mode disabled`.

Use `show current-fw-<name>/<fw-name> [fw-version] [expected-fw-version] [fw-status]` (also keyed as <card-name>-<port-name>, <card-name>.<slot-name> or <chassis-name>-<slot-name>). It compares `fw-version`, the current firmware version, against `expected-fw-version`, the expected version, both Strings of length 0..32. `fw-status` gives the verdict with values current (current firmware is up-to-date), not-current (current firmware is not up-to-date against the expected one) and unavailable (firmware status information is currently unavailable); the default is unavailable. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode. Examples: `show current-fw` lists all, `show current-fw-1-3/DCO_1` shows one card component.

`download` accepts filetype values crl (a CRL in PEM format), database (a previously uploaded database), file (any file to the file-system), krp (key replacement package), local-certificate (PKCS#12 with password-protected private key, or PKCS#7 if pending-import), peer-certificate (X.509v3 PKCS#12), script (a CLI script), swimage (downloads a manifest file then all files belonging to a SW image), and trusted-certificate (X.509v3 PKCS#7 Root or Intermediate CA). The system automatically stores the downloaded file in an appropriate place; there is no need to provide a local storage location. The exception is filetype 'file', where `destination` may be omitted (default directory, original name), a file-name only, a relative path or an absolute path, and you must have write access to it; use `show transfer` to see the default storage directory. A downloaded database is stored as a db-instance=temp database, overwriting any existing temp. Source is a URL (ftp, sftp, scp, http, https, file) or a pre-configured file-server plus path; non-secure ftp/http need secure-mode disabled.

Use `show downloaded-image-<manifest-file>/<name> [signature]`, which retrieves information about downloaded image files. The `signature` attribute is the downloaded software image file signature, a String of length 0..1024. The key is the manifest file (String, length 0..256) plus `name`, the name of the downloaded software image (String, length 0..256). Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. `show downloaded-image` lists all downloaded software image files.

`show downloads` shows the list of downloads. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Related commands: `show downloaded-image-<manifest-file>/<name> [signature]` for information about downloaded image files including the image signature, `show manifest` for the downloaded manifest file and its information, `show sw-management` for software locations, activity and downloads, and `show transfer-status filetype` to check progress of a download started asynchronously with `download -a`.
